title: Indicator vs No Indicator
hook: Your eyes first. Then check your work.

launchpad.outcome: Mark the chart with the indicator off, compare with the indicator, then with Dayli, and choose how you want the indicator to assist you.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Can I explain the read without the indicator?

slides.headline: Indicator off. Find the PIL yourself.
slides.line: This is the 1H. Price rallied, then pulled back.
slides.do: Tap the price of the 1H swing high price pulled back from. That’s your PIL.
slides.wrong: Not quite. Look for the highest swing, the one the pullback started from.
slides.right: Yes. The 1H swing price pulled back from. That’s the level the session will test.

slides.headline: Now switch the indicator on.
slides.line: It marked a different level: a smaller swing inside the rally.

options.label: The indicator’s level
options.say: The indicator anchored on an internal swing. A difference isn’t automatically your mistake.

options.label: The 1H swing
options.sub: The level price pulled back from
options.say: Yes. The 1H swing comes first because it’s the level on the map.

slides.headline: How should the indicator help you?
slides.line: Your choice is saved. You can change it any time.

options.label: Show it after I mark
options.sub: Recommended: my eyes first, then check my work
options.say: Saved. You mark first, then the indicator checks you.

options.label: Show it from the start
options.sub: Faster, but it can do the thinking for me
options.say: Saved. Keep checking that you can explain the read without it.

slides.dayli: The indicator should make your process faster, not replace your eyes.

takeaways: A difference isn’t automatically your mistake. Reason it through.
Default: indicator revealed after your analysis.
remember: The indicator should make your process faster, not replace your eyes.
